newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds stronger on back of U.S. Treasuries.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds stronger on back of U.S. Treasuries.

text.p: Irish government bonds looked stronger in thin late trade on Friday on the back of a continued good tone to U.S. Treasuries, dealers said.
"We opened a touch better on the back of a strong U.S. performance overnight and have largely held on to those gains," one dealer said.

"We are 131 basis points over bunds in the five-year area and 92 basis points over bunds in the 10-year area, good value really. At this stage, people are closing their books before the year-end," the dealer added.
By 1537 GMT, the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 had gained 15 pence to 101.50 to yield 6.03 percent while the eight percent bond due 2001 had firmed 30 pence to 108.75 to yield 6.72 percent.
